paragraphs: This occupation uses drilling equipment to produce holes, cores or wells according to the project. Consider whether you want to learn about field equipment, accurate records and team coordination; specific duties vary by project.

A first exploration can start with interest in outdoor, equipment-based work and a willingness to learn about record accuracy, field conditions and employer training. You do not need prior drilling-tool or parameter-setting competence to try the paper case.

Needs caution: if you expect this job to be indoors or to involve only pressing buttons and watching gauges, or you are unwilling to wear protective equipment and follow edge, electrical, hoisting, rotating part, high-pressure line, dust, noise, and wellhead safety requirements (drilling without a stable site or warning barriers, approaching moving parts contrary to guarding and operating procedures, not adjusting drilling speed and air pressure according to the geotechnical conditions, not handling in-hole accidents and dropped tools per the procedures, not disposing of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil as required), or you find it hard to keep precision and patience under repetitive operations and long field hours and the pressure of dealing with downhole problems, then the actual work experience usually does not match the expectation.

Start with the complete fictional A/B record-checking case below. Compare depths, sample identifiers and receipt fields, write a question list and review it against the reference checks. Use it to explore your interest in documentation, not to prove field competence.

Decision center: whether the task and site and geotechnical conditions and equipment can be turned into a drilling and well completion and record chain that the team leader and geology and inspection can all take up and verify.

The work combines field equipment, checking and records. O*NET respondents reported all-weather outdoor work daily at 79%, noise daily at 65% and whole-body vibration daily at 42%; these are group responses, not a prediction of your exposure.

Compare actual work rather than similar names. Derricks and mud pumps, oil-well service, pile driving and general construction have distinct but sometimes overlapping tasks. Training and project authority do not transfer automatically with a job title.

For a first exploration, compare the complete record exercise with the work described here. Ask an employer or training provider about equipment, outdoor conditions, supervision and required preparation. PPE does not make contact with moving machinery safe; actual work follows the applicable guarding and operating procedures.

Actual tolerance of noise, vibration, weather and physical demands cannot be established by a paper task or personality result. If you explore further, ask a suitable provider about supervised observation or training and the relevant job requirements.

All exercises on this page use fictional materials; real drilling operations and in-hole operations and blasting and wellhead and electrical and field work must be undertaken by organizations and personnel with the corresponding training and qualifications that follow the regulations and standards of the relevant jurisdiction and this project's requirements; individuals must not exceed authorization to issue geological, engineering, environmental, safety, or compliance conclusions externally, and this page does not constitute geological, engineering, environmental, safety, or legal advice.

For this occupation, project inputs can include the required hole, sampling or well output, ground information, equipment and site conditions. Outputs and records depend on the particular drilling task; not every job includes every coring, well-development or testing activity.

Judgment one: whether the task and hole position and depth and diameter are verified clearly — checking the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements against the task sheet and geological data and site conditions, rather than starting to drill from impression.

Judgment two: whether the site and pipelines and buried objects and slopes are safe — confirming site bearing capacity and leveling and outrigger stability and overhead lines and underground pipelines and buried objects and slopes and edge conditions, rather than positioning without checking.
Drilling work involves monitoring progress and following the project’s equipment, design and operating requirements.

Judgment four: whether hole depth and position and verticality and cores and samples are in place — verifying the hole depth and position and verticality and taking cores and samples and logging and submitting them for testing as required, rather than recording carelessly.
The crew may coordinate with geological, surveying, equipment and safety personnel; the job title alone does not define approval or sign-off authority.
Safety and environmental responsibilities include following the applicable project arrangements and reporting equipment or downhole problems to the responsible personnel.

The work of earth drillers, except oil and gas, can be divided into three connected but independent work surfaces. The first is task and site and positioning and preparation: study the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements from the task sheet and geological data, survey the site and access and water and power and working face and verify overhead lines and underground pipelines and buried objects and slopes and edge conditions, level and stabilize the site and position and level the truck-mounted or trailer-mounted rig and stabilize the outriggers and extend the mast, assemble and inspect the rig and tools and bits and rods and well completion equipment, and confirm the mud or flushing and dust removal and waste residue and waste oil and wastewater disposal plan and protective equipment and warning measures. The second is drilling and sampling and well completion: select bits and rods according to the geotechnical and strata conditions and operate to control and stabilize the machine and align the tools and start, stop, and adjust drilling, adjust air pressure and rotation speed and down pressure according to the rock or concrete type and add or remove rods and change bits, operate equipment to flush cuttings or blow out dust from the hole, verify the hole position and depth and verticality and align the drilling position, observe returns and changes in drilling speed and record the geological horizons and drilling progress by stratum, take cores and samples and check the cores and submit them for testing, drill for blasting or grouting or anchoring or foundations, and for well completion install the well casing and screen and filter material and sealing and install the pump and other in-well facilities and flush and wash and disinfect and conduct pumping tests, perform routine maintenance and upgrade equipment (replacing parts, hardfacing bits, lubricating machinery), and fish out dropped equipment. The third is records and safety and environmental protection and handover: record the geological horizons and drilling progress and samples and equipment maintenance and in-hole anomalies, dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil per the procedures and restore the site, inspect the protection and warning and electrical and hoisting and rotating part and high-pressure line conditions, and hand over with the team leader and geology and inspection and the back office. All three work surfaces proceed within the task sheet and geological data and geotechnical conditions and drilling rig and tool and safety and environmental procedures.
Task and site and positioning and preparation

Study the task sheet and geological data to determine the hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements → survey the site and pipelines and slopes and level and stabilize → position and level the rig and stabilize the outriggers and extend the mast → assemble and inspect the drilling tools and well completion equipment and disposal plan

Executable checklist of hole position and depth and diameter and drilling tool selection and site and safety key points, positioning and leveling and outrigger stabilization and warning and protection records, and drilling tool and bit and equipment inspection records
Drilling and sampling and well completion

Select bits and rods according to the geotechnical conditions → operate to stabilize and align and adjust drilling parameters → flush and blow out dust and verify hole depth and position and verticality → observe returns and record strata and take cores and samples for testing → install well casing and screen and sealing and wash the well and conduct pumping tests

Drilling and sampling logging records completed by task and geotechnical conditions, hole depth and position and verticality and strata records, well completion and well washing and pumping test and disinfection records, and equipment maintenance and in-hole anomaly handling records
Records and safety and environmental protection and handover

Record strata and progress and samples and equipment and anomalies → dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil per the procedures and restore the site → inspect protection and warning and electrical and hoisting and rotating part conditions → report anomalies and hand over

Where are the boundaries between this page's occupation and adjacent positions such as oil and gas drilling and derrick and service units, pile drivers, construction equipment operators, and construction labor?

Compare these occupations by their work objects, equipment, outputs and actual responsibilities. Derrick work centers on derricks, drill-pipe handling and mud-circulation pumps; construction labor covers varied site tasks and tools. Task overlap does not establish interchangeable training or authority.
Core purpose

Turn the task and site and geotechnical conditions and equipment into a borehole result that meets the hole position and depth and verticality and coring or well completion requirements: task and hole position clear, site and pipelines and slopes safe, drilling tools and parameters on a documented basis, sampling and well completion and records in place, and safety and environmental requirements held.

Adjacent jobs focus on oil and gas drilling; derricks and mud-circulation pumps; well servicing; pile installation; construction equipment; or varied physical construction work. The actual purpose depends on the job.
Main objects and basis

The objects are the task sheet and hole position and depth and diameter and coring or well completion requirements, site and access and water and power and working face and slope and underground pipeline and buried objects, drilling rigs and tools and bits and rods and well completion equipment, geotechnical and groundwater and strata information, and sampling logging and safety and environmental records; the basis is the task sheet and geological data and geotechnical conditions and drilling rig and tool and safety and environmental procedures.

Relevant equipment and inputs may include oil-well rigs and drilling fluids, derricks and mud pumps, well-service equipment, piles, construction machinery, and hand or power tools. Compare the actual task and equipment rather than assuming identical procedures.
Core process

Task and site and positioning and preparation → drilling and sampling and well completion (selection and drilling and flushing and verification and coring and casing installation and well washing) → records and safety and environmental protection and handover and anomaly reporting.

Adjacent work includes oil and gas drilling and fluid circulation, derrick and mud-pump work, well servicing, pile driving, construction-equipment operations, and varied construction tasks using hand or power tools.
Main outputs

Drilling and sampling logging records completed by task and geotechnical conditions, hole depth and position and verticality and strata records, well completion and well washing and pumping test and disinfection records, equipment maintenance and in-hole anomaly handling records, and safety and environmental and handover records.

Outputs vary by job and may include drilling, derrick or pump work, well servicing, pile installation, equipment records and varied construction work. An occupation title does not establish every duty.
Responsible parties

This occupation bears execution responsibility for selecting drilling tools and controlling drilling according to the task and geotechnical conditions and for coring and sampling and casing installation and well completion and records; responsibility for geology and engineering design and blasting operations and well condition safety and environmental acceptance and acceptance is borne by the owner and design unit and construction unit and competent authorities and personnel with the corresponding qualifications according to regulations and standards.

Responsibilities for operation, supervision, quality confirmation and sign-off depend on the actual employer, contract and project arrangements. Occupational definitions do not establish one contractor or role as the universal responsible party.
Collaboration and supervision

Collaborate with the team leader and geology and surveying and inspection and the back office and equipment repair and safety and environmental personnel, and adjust priorities according to the task and hole depth and schedule and sampling milestones; immediately report in-hole anomalies and equipment hazards and safety and environmental problems and matters beyond authorization.

Coordination depends on the equipment, site and process. When comparing jobs, check team interfaces, assigned tasks and training; drilling-team experience does not establish authority to operate in another role.
Conclusion boundaries

Do not enter and position without verifying pipelines and buried objects and slopes and site bearing capacity, do not drill without leveling and stabilizing outriggers and setting warning barriers, do not touch rotating parts and high-pressure lines and transmission parts without protective gear or without shutting down the machine, do not select bits and adjust parameters without regard to the geotechnical conditions, do not fail to handle in-hole accidents and dropped tools and stuck pipe and water inflow per the procedures, do not fail to dispose of mud and waste oil and wastewater and spoil as required, do not conceal or delay reporting in-hole anomalies and equipment hazards and safety and environmental problems, and do not issue geological or engineering or environmental or safety or compliance conclusions externally beyond authorization.

The boundaries of adjacent positions are determined by their respective task sheets and geological data and standards and qualifications and the regulations of the relevant jurisdiction; similar job titles do not mean the duties are interchangeable.

Order No. 35 as amended by Order No. 78 applies to geological exploration of metal and non-metal minerals and does not apply to exploration in producing mines; Article 7 requires a safety permit for construction units undertaking drilling or exploration by excavation within that scope, Article 8 requires written reports, Article 9 covers systems, and Articles 18/19 cover protection, rescue, and emergency response. Article 11 requires special personnel to receive dedicated training, assessment, and the corresponding certificate; Article 12 requires personnel undertaking exploration by excavation to receive at least 72h initially and 20h of annual retraining, and this is not extended to all surface drillers. Article 15 requires a special safety chapter and review for the design of exploration by excavation, and this is not extended to general water wells or all earth boring. The 2017 geological exploration qualification approval has been cancelled, and a 2025 public reply from the Ministry of Natural Resources confirms that solid mineral exploration units and personnel have no such access threshold; the old 'qualification certificate' can no longer be listed as a current general condition, and this does not exempt safety permits or special operation certification. The current reporting materials, competent authorities, and local processing are verified separately. AQ2004-2005 platform current/mandatory; clause 1 covers Chinese geological exploration (excluding oil and gas geological exploration) and explicitly does not apply to using the technology in other industries, so the U.S. code scope is not fully mapped onto the standard scope. Actually read: 4.5 requires geological exploration units to provide field survival and self- and mutual-rescue skills training at least once every two years for field personnel; the project team provides safety education before departure for fieldwork each year or before changing regions, 4.7 protective equipment, 4.8 health examinations; 10.1/10.2 rig foundation and drill frame installation and handling, 10.4.1 equipment protection inspection before spudding, 10.4.2 prohibition of cleaning, disassembling, or repairing and of stepping over drive belts while rotating, 10.4.3 shutting down before repairing high-pressure hoses; 10.5.2 in-hole accidents are handled by the rig team leader or an experienced technician under dedicated command while others evacuate, and 10.7.8 electrical repair requires disconnecting the power and posting a warning tag or assigning an attendant. Specific designs/equipment/new versions of cited standards are verified separately, and this page is not an operating manual.

Are the sampling and logging and submission for testing coordination with geology and surveying and inspection and the hole depth and position verification and well completion acceptance milestones completed by task and verifiable?

Record hole position and depth and verticality and strata and sampling and well completion and equipment maintenance data according to the task and this project's systems and complete handover; records should agree with sampling and progress and safety materials to facilitate verification; in-hole anomalies and dropped tools and stuck pipe and water inflow are handled per the procedures with records kept.

Articles 44/45 of the Chinese Work Safety Law require the unit to inform workers of hazards and provide compliant PPE, and Article 54 allows refusal of illegal commands or forced risk-taking; Article 55 allows stopping or taking necessary emergency measures and then evacuating when personal danger is immediate, without requiring registration, reporting, or approval beforehand; Articles 57/58 require following procedures, correct PPE, and training, and Article 59 requires hazards to be reported immediately to on-site safety management or the unit head. paragraphs: Rotary drill operators, oil and gas (47-5012.00)
Operate oil and gas drilling equipment, connect drill pipe, monitor drilling, and work with drilling-fluid circulation and casing equipment.

The work concerns oil and gas wells. This occupation covers drilling, coring and water-well work outside oil and gas extraction. Equipment experience may be relevant, but procedures, hazards and responsibilities require separate checks.
Explore this direction if oil and gas drilling interests you; compare it with this occupation if your interests lie in groundwater, geological coring or other non-oil-and-gas drilling.
Derrick operators, oil and gas (47-5011.00)
Rig or operate derricks and operate, inspect and maintain pumps and related equipment that circulate drilling mud through a well.

The focus includes derricks, drill-pipe handling and mud-circulation equipment, rather than all wellhead operations. This occupation instead concerns non-oil-and-gas drilling, coring and well construction.
Explore this direction if derricks, drill-pipe handling and mud-pump systems interest you, and check the equipment and safety training required by the target job.
Service unit operators, oil and gas (47-5013.00)
The focus is servicing oil and gas wells and carrying out work inside them. This occupation focuses on non-oil-and-gas drilling, coring and water wells.
Explore specific jobs if well servicing, obstruction removal and fishing equipment interest you; drilling experience alone does not establish competence for those operations.
Pile driver operators (47-2072.00)
The focus is installing and driving piles. This occupation focuses on drilling, coring or water wells. Similar-looking equipment does not imply identical processes or quality requirements.
Compare this direction if pile installation and foundation construction interest you; explore this occupation if drilling, geological samples and water wells interest you more.
Operating engineers and other construction equipment operators (47-2073.00)
The equipment and construction tasks are broader; this occupation specializes in drilling rigs, drilling tools, coring and well-construction processes.
Explore specific equipment jobs if earthmoving, grading, excavation or paving interests you; the occupation title does not establish qualification to operate every machine.
Construction laborers (47-2061.00)
Duties are broad, and some tools and drilling tasks overlap. Construction laborers are not limited to carrying and cleanup, nor are all drilling or sampling-equipment tasks excluded.
Explore specific construction-laborer jobs if varied site tasks appeal to you; compare this occupation if you prefer specializing in non-oil-and-gas drilling, coring or water wells.

facts.display_value: National exact wage gap for this occupation in China. NBS2025 construction non-private 92036/ private 66275, and scientific and technical services non-private 182064/ private 83560 yuan per year (on the current Chinese and English original page table 5: 2025=83560, 2024=82387) are pre-tax industry averages respectively; construction/geological/geotechnical positions may be relevant but the unit classification must be verified, and these are not the occupational median/starting pay/monthly wage; they cover 5+ urban legal entities and exclude self-employment and freelance work, and do not exclude all unit piece-rate/part-time/labor dispatch workers. Order No. 35 as amended by Order No. 78 applies to geological exploration of metal and non-metal minerals and does not apply to exploration in producing mines; Article 7 requires a safety permit for drilling and excavation-based geological exploration construction units within that scope, Article 8 requires written reports, Article 9 covers systems, and Articles 18/19 cover protection, rescue, and emergency response. Article 11 requires special personnel to receive dedicated training, assessment, and the corresponding certificate; Article 12 requires excavation-based geological exploration personnel to receive at least 72h initially and 20h of annual retraining, and this is not extended to all surface drillers. Article 15 requires a special safety chapter and review for excavation-based geological exploration design, and this is not extended to general water wells or all earth boring. The 2017 geological exploration qualification approval has been cancelled, and a 2025 public reply from the Ministry of Natural Resources confirms that solid mineral exploration units and personnel have no such access threshold; the old 'qualification certificate' can no longer be listed as a current general condition, and this does not exempt safety permits or special operation certification. The current reporting materials, competent authorities, and local processing are verified separately.

subject.name: Earth drillers, except oil and gas
subject.summary: Earth drillers operate drilling equipment for water wells, mineral exploration, soil investigations and construction or mining holes. Duties vary by project: coring, well development and drilling blast holes are possible tasks, not a requirement that every worker performs all of them. In mainland China, the work overlaps with geological exploration drillers (4-08-07-01); project scope, employer training and applicable work-safety requirements need separate checks.
